change_note: COHERENCE FIX (pv.findings.md, Med): precondition asserted 'back-office comms available' while step 3 deliberately exercises the comms-UNAVAILABLE path ('Failed to retrieve locations from server') — a direct contradiction. Dropped the comms-availability claim from the precondition entirely; comms state is now scoped only where it matters (step 3's own WHEN clause already says 'with comms unavailable'), so the case no longer asserts two contradictory starting states. Behaviour (view/change home location from a server-provided list; reboot required to apply) is grounded on the Overflow Technician Menu annotations. The exact fail-screen message text ('Failed to retrieve locations from server') is not itemised verbatim in the annotations — only that a distinct 'Location Settings - Fail' screen exists — so left as-is (pre-existing suite wording, not newly invented here) rather than asserted as newly grounded.

**GAP** — a PV 'Operating Times' schedule feature (governing scheduled out-of-service/in-service transitions) is not found in the reviewed Technician Menu design annotations (PV Technician Menu enumerates only Login/Location/Software Version/Brightness/Force Comms/Network/Configuration Version/Audio/Sign Off) or in FBD-100304; confirm on the live system before running
refs: knowledge/flows/pv-flow-annotations.md (Technician Menu - Platform Validator screen list — no Operating Times screen enumerated)
citations: knowledge/flows/pv-flow-annotations.md 'Technician Menu - Platform Validator' section lists 24 screens across Login/Location/Software Version/Brightness/Force Communications/Network Interfaces/Configuration Version/Audio/Sign Off — no Operating Times / scheduled service-window screen among them
FBD-100304 (TFTS System Diagram Roadmap) — no scheduled operating-hours / operating-times device configuration found in the sections reviewed
change_note: GROUNDING: this case's entire premise — a technician-configurable PV operating-times schedule that drives automatic out-of-service/in-service transitions — is not confirmed in either the Overflow Technician Menu design (a fairly complete 24-screen enumeration for the PV Technician Menu that does not include this) or FBD-100304. Not found = not necessarily untrue (the Overflow extraction may not be exhaustive), so marked GAP rather than condemning the case outright. Drafted as a new gap-register question.

Marked each with a GAP rather than deleting — the case may still be correct (Overflow extraction may not be exhaustive) but nothing here currently traces to a source. Drafted as a new gap-register question; also flagged as a candidate case-structure review (3 unrelated Technician Menu features bundled in one case) for a future consolidation pass, not addressed here.

steps.content: **WHEN** you leave a page with no input until it times out
steps.expected: **THEN** the PV returns to the Technician Menu home screen

steps.content: **WHEN** the inactivity period then elapses on the home screen
steps.expected:
**THEN** the PV auto signs the technician off
**GAP** — the accompanying tone and the exact two-stage timeout sequence (page-idle→home screen, then a separate home-screen inactivity period→auto sign-off) are not confirmed in the reviewed Technician Menu design annotations, which document only a 3-second/Enter-key timeout on the PIN-entry field; confirm on the live system before running
**AND** the sign-off is recorded in the CloudFare activity log

refs: knowledge/flows/pv-flow-annotations.md (Technician Menu general annotations — PIN-field timeout only)
citations: knowledge/flows/pv-flow-annotations.md 'Technician Menu' annotations describe only a PIN-entry-field redirect timeout ('after 3 seconds or by pressing Enter') and an 'error message disappears after a short timeout' on Incorrect Details — no page-level home-screen timeout or a separate home-screen-inactivity auto-sign-off-with-tone sequence
change_note: GROUNDING: the general concept (Technician Menu security timeout signs the technician off on inactivity) is plausible and common practice, but the specific two-stage mechanism and audible tone asserted in step 2 aren't confirmed anywhere reviewed — only a narrower PIN-field-specific timeout is documented. Kept step 1 as-is (page→home timeout is a lower-risk, more generic claim) and added a GAP marker only on the more specific/riskier claim in step 2 (the tone + the exact sequencing) rather than blocking the whole case. Drafted as a new gap-register question.

refs: TIBU-24260, TIBU-26053, TIBU-25548, TIBU-26054, TIBU-26531, FBD-100263, gap-register Q23
citations: FBD-100263 (CloudFare Asset Tracking Reports) V4.00 paras 187/327/403: 'SIM ID' is a real, named field in the Asset Tracking / Asset Manager reporting spec — not invented

gap-register.md Q23 (ANSWERED): PV confirmed to have real cellular/SIM hardware (REQ-2746.0 old-suite failover cases; TIBU-24428's QA-passed Ethernet⇌cellular matrix; TIBU-29191/C4091908 show the Technician Menu Network Settings screen displaying both an Ethernet and a Cellular interface) — a SIM ID being reported to CloudFare is therefore consistent with the hardware, reversing pv.findings.md's earlier 'PV may be Ethernet-only' doubt
change_note: RESOLVES pv.findings.md Med finding (needs-confirmation): step 2 asserts the PV reports a 'SIM ID' to CloudFare Asset Manager. At the time of that finding the PV's comms model was still disputed (gap-register Q9, since reversed by Q23) as possibly Ethernet-only, which would make a 'SIM ID' incongruous. Q23 now confirms the PV has real cellular/SIM hardware, and FBD-100263 confirms 'SIM ID' is the actual asset-tracking field name (not a stand-in for some other identifier) — so no wording change was needed, only the Refs backfill grounding both facts. No content change to preface/preconds/steps.
